full_judgment:
A K Badrul Huq, J: Can an order not being a case decided and not determining a matter by a decision be the subject matter of challenge by a party to a civil proceeding in invoking this Court's civil revisional jurisdiction on laying a petition under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is the principal .question which requires an answer in the Rule arising out of a petition under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. An order dated November 30. 1999 recorded by the learned Assistant Judge, Second Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 356 of 1999 fixing 2.1.2000 for hearing of ad-interim injunction on allowing a petition presented by the defendants for adjournment of hearing has been the subject matter of civil revision petition under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure whereupon Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the order dated 30.11.1999 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Second Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 356 of 1999 should not be set aside. 

 3. The portrayal of essential facts forming the background of this civil revision petition may succinctly be stated which are as follows: 

 The petitioner of civil revision petition as plaintiff on 17.11.1999 laid a suit being Title Suit No. 356 of 1999 in the Second Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka for a declaration that the defendant (opposite party) could not act or represent himself as Chairman and Managing Director of the plaintiff-Company and the purported attempt by the defendant to act as Chairman and Managing Director of the plaintiff company is illegal, malafide and void and also for a decree of permanent injunction restraining the defendant (opposite party) from acting as Chairman and Managing Director of the plaintiff-company. Averments made in the plaint is that plaintiff is a Public Limited Company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1913 having its registered office at 10/22, Eastern Plaza, Sonargaon Road, Dhaka. Defendant is a share-holder. The affairs of the company were mainly looked-after by Md. Abdul Ahad as Executive Director and Sirajul Islam Chowdhury as Managing Director. On sudden death of M.A. Ahad on 8.11.1995 the whole operational side of the company was left unattended and in-spite of repeated request the former Managing Director of the Company (defendant-opposite party) failed to take any initiative to reconstitute the Board of Directors of the Company. To resolve the dispute over the management and functioning of the company a joint meeting was held on 6A 1.1997 at Hotel Purbani International between the defendant and the representative sons of late M A Ahad in the presence of Mr. Abdul Mannan and Dr. A K M Ali, Advocates. A memorandum of under-standing had been prepared which was witnessed by the above two learned Advocates. Defendant.refused to honour the Memorandum of understanding dated 6.11.1997 and he started producing false financial statements and misappropriating company's fund at the cost of company's business and reputation. Thereafter, in an  Extraordinary General. Meeting on requisition held on 15.11.99, the members present by unanimous decision removed the Chairman and Managing Director of the company from the office of Chairman and Managing Director and in his place appointed Mr. Altaf Ahmed as the company's new Chairman and Managing Director. Defendant refused to honour the decision taken in Extraordinary General Meeting and started representing himself as the Chairman and Managing Director of the company. 

 4. The plaintiff, along with the plaint, almost upon same averments made in the plaint presented an application for temporary injunction under Order 39, Rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for an order of temporary injunction restraining the defendant from acting or representing himself as Chairman and Managing Director of the plaintiff company and pending hearing an order of ad-interim injunction was sought in" the terms of the petition for temporary injunction. 

 7. The plaintiff, thereafter, by presenting an application under Order 39, Rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure prayed for an order of temporary injunction. The defendant also sought an adjournment and the court fixed 29.11.1999 to hear the defendant. On 29.11.1999 the plaintiff presented another application for ad-Interim injunction under the provision of Order- 39 Rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The copy was received by the defendant with serious objection. The court fixed 30.11.1999 for hearing on the above two applications dated 28.11.1999 and 29.11.1999. The court also directed the defendant to file written objection if any. On 30.11.99 the plaintiff filed hajira and the defendant by presenting an application prayed for time for filing written objection which was hotly opposed by the plaintiff. The defendant by way of an another application prayed for adjournment of the hearing. The court allowed the same and fixed 2.1.2000 for hearing. 

 8. The plaintiff felt dissatisfied with the said order dated 30.11.1999 and invoked this Court's civil revisional jurisdiction on laying a petition under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule. 

 9. Basic grounds pressed into service in the civil revision petition are as follow: 

 (i) For the ends of justice and to prevent abuse of the process of the court the learned Assistant Judge should have disposed of the application filed under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and by the impugned order adjourning the hearing, the learned Court committed an error of law resulting an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice. 

 10. The statements contained in the civil revision petition had been controverted from the side of the defendant-opposite party on presentation of a counter affidavit wherein it is stated, inter alias that ad-interim injunction is discretionary jurisdiction of the trial court under Order 39, Rule 1 and 2 of the Code and not of High Court Division to grant ad-interim injunction. Late Mr. M.A. Ahad was not Managing Director of the company but was only as Executive Director and, even after his death on 8.11.1995 long 56 years have passed without any urgency for changing the Managing Director through an ad-interim injunction. The so-called resolution passed in the Extraordinary General Meeting on 15.11.1999 is a paper work for the purpose of the suit and law does not allow the removal of the existing Managing Director and appointment of a new Managing Director and Chairman. Further statement is that time being inadequate the defendant applied for time for filing written objection and the court adjourned hearing till the next earliest working day of the court on 02.1.2000. Positive stand taken is that the impugned order was not such an order which could bi interfered with by this Court in its revisional jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 (1) The order of not recording any order of ad-interim injunction amounted to refusal by implication and the same though being appealable under Order 43 Rule 1 (R), of the Code of Civil Procedure the civil court having been in vacation, the plaintiff-petitioner had no other alternative but to invoke this Court's revisional jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the civil revision petition is, thus, maintainable. Reliance had been placed in support of the contention on Explanation V to section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and an autlfority in Ghulam Muhammad Vs. Sultan Mahmud and other is, 15 DLR SC 172. 

 (ii) This Court to secure justice and to prevent abuse process of the court got inherent power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to record any order which it deems fit and proper inducting granting an injunction and fact and circumstances of the case demands issuance of an ad-interim injunction for the smooth functioning of the company. 

 12. Repelling the said contention it is strenuously pressed from the side of the defendant-opposite party that the civil revision petition under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not at all entertain able against the order recorded by the learned Assistant Judge when he did not dispose of the matter through a decision. Time was too short on the part of the defendant-opposite party to present written objection and as such prayer for time was sought before the court which was rightly allowed and no illegality had been committed by the learned court in allowing the time prayer of the defendant-opposite party and fixing 2.1.2000 for hearing, it is further submitted. 

 13. For the purpose of appreciating the rival contentions addressed before me the provisions contained in Explanation V to section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure may conveniently be noticed and considered. 

 14. Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure is as follows: 

 "11. No court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties, or between parties under whom they or any of them claim, litigating under the same title, in a court competent to try such subsequent suit or the suit in which such issue has been subsequently raised, and has been heard and finally decided by such Court." 

 15. Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure enshrines that no court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties or between parties under whom they or any of them claim, litigating under the same title, in a court competent to try such subsequent suit or. the suit in which such issue has been subsequently raised, and has been heard and finally decided by such Court. 

 18. On a reading of section 11 of the Code it, thus, appears that it relates to a suit or issue decided in a suit and the relief so coined in Explanation V is a relief claimed in a suit. 

 19. Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure had undergone two amendments after he Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908) come into force, one by Law Reforms ordinance, 1978 which came into force on 1st of June, 1979 an Second one by the Law forms Ordinance of 1983 which came into orce on 7th of September, 1983. 

 24. From a reading of section 115 it has become manifestly clear that for interference by the High Court Division in exercise of revisional authority under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the order itself must be a case decided and that case is to be decided by a decision. The word "decision" is 'wide enough to include both final and interlocutory. Every matter required to be decided by a court judiciously on application of mind  with reasons in support thereof would he a case decided for the purpose of exercising revisional jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. To put it differently. section 115 of the Code would be attracted if a court subordinate to the High Court Division has given a decision in respect of any state of facts after judicially considering the same . There had been a conflict of judicial opinion as to the meaning of the phrase "case decided" but the controversy was resolved by the majority of the Full Bench of Seven Judges of the High Court, Karachi in S. Zafar Ahmed Vs. Abdul Khaliq PLD 1964 (West Pakistan)' Karachi 149 wherein position has been correctly stated that section 115 would be attracted if a court subordinate to the High Court has given a decision in respect of any state of facts after judicially considering the same. The Supreme Court of Pakistan in Bashir Ahmad Khan Vs. Qaiser Ali Khan and others, PLD 1973 SC 507 relied upon the above stated authority and held that if a court subordinate to the High Court renders its decision in respect of any state of facts after judicially considering the same, it will amount to case decided. I do not see that the said enunciation of law had been over ruled by any other authority of any other High Courts and apex Courts. 

 25. The words "decision" had not been defined ii the Code of Civil Procedure. Sub-section 9 a section 2 of the Code enjoins that "judgment" means the statement given by the Judge of the grounds of a decree or order. Sub-section 14 of section 2 of the Code enshrines that "order" means the formal expression of any decision of a civil court which is not a decree. 

 27. In Corpus Juris Secundum, Volume 26 "decision" has been said to be one necessarily involving a dispute and reaching of a conclusion. In the civil law generally it means the determination of a question, the final order which disposed of a suit or cause. 

 29. Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure runs thus: 

 30. Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure enjoins that nothing in the Code shall be deemed to limit or otherwise affect the inherent power of the Court to make such orders as may be necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the Court. Section 151 of the Code does not formulate any new doctrine but only a legislative recognition of the well known doctrine and principle that every court has inherent power to act ex debito justitiae and to do that real justice for the administration of which alone it exist. Every court including the High Court Division is possessed of such inherent power as may be necessary to do complete justice between the parties according to varying circumstances which may arise in the cause of administration of justice. Inherent power has not been conferred on the court but it has a power inherent in the court by virtue of its duty to do justice between the parties. The words "as may be necessary for the ends of justice" appearing in section 151 of the Code gives inherent power to the High Court Division also to interfere with the order of the subordinate court and record any order to secure the ends of justice. 

 32. I shall now direct myself to deal with the first branch of contention pressed into service from the side of the plaintiff-petitioner. It had already been stated that in -order to attract section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure it is to be shown that a matter which has been directly and substantially in issue in the previous suit cannot be re-opened and relit gated. In the case in hand no issue was finally decided in any previously instituted suit between the contending parties. Explanation is also not attracted in as much as prayer sought in the application for ad-interim injunction under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not fall within the mischief of Explanation V to section 11 of the Code. Ghulam Muhammad Vs. Sultan Mahmud and others 15 DLR SC 172 got no manner applicable in the facts and circumstances of the case in hand. It is to be borne in mind that a decision is only an authority for what it actually decides and it cannot be quoted for a proposition that may seem to follow from it  Every judgment must be read applicable to the particular facts proved or assumed to be proved. The generality of expression that may be found cannot he intended to be exposition of whole law but must be regarded as governed or qualified by the particular facts of the case in which such expression occurs . 

 33. Let me now turn to the maintainability aspect of the civil revision petition under section 115 of the Code. On a mere perusal of the order under challenge dated 30.11.1999 it appears that the learned Assistant Judge did not determine and decide the petition for ad-interim injunction laid under section 151 of the Code but merely granted adjournment on allowing the petition presented by the defendant-opposite party and fixed 2.01.2000 for hearing of the injunction matter. It, thus, cannot be said that matter was decided by the learned Assistant Judge by a decision and the said order cannot be at all characterised to be a decision. I am of this considered view that the order under challenge having not a case decided and not a decision, the civil revision petition against the said order is not maintainable. The first branch of contention having been without any force, is ruled out. 

 34. The second branch Of contention advanced from the side of the plaintiff-petitioner now requires to be answered. It cannot be disputed that the power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not a new power conferred upon the court by the Code of Civil Procedure and it is very much inherent in the court and it can record any order to secure ends of justice and to prevent abuse of process of court. Now the question comes whether this Court will come in aid of the plaintiff-petitioner to record any order of ad-interim injunction in exercise of its inherent power under section 151 of the Code. True it is that this court can record any order in exercise of inherent power but the power inherent in this Court is to be exercised very sparingly, in rarest of rare cases, if circumstances so demand and where it is manifested that there has been gross abuse of process of the court and interference of court has become imperative. It is also true that the learned Assistant Judge was required to record any order, no matter he granted ad-interim injunction or refused the same. 

 37. Before parting I am inclined to record an observation that now-a days it is seen that Whenever any party to a suit or proceeding presents an application either for temporary injunction or for an order of attachment before judgment or for appointment of receiver or any other matter, the learned Judge of the subordinate judiciary does not record any positive order either allowing or rejecting the same which is required to record. The procedure adopted by the learned Judge is highly disapproved. 

 38. Resultantly, the Rule arising out of civil revision petition stands discharged.
